Respond with:

questions: You have three hours of peak creative energy today. Your editor needs a structural revision by morning, but you've just felt the somatic 'click' on a difficult image that's been resisting you for weeks. What costs you more to leave behind?

Your most formally experimental piece is being offered publication if you add explanatory notes. The notes would make it accessible but destroy the deliberate strangeness. What do you experience in your chest when you imagine each version?

You're in a workshop where someone interprets your work in a way that reveals something you didn't know you were hiding. They want to discuss it directly. What does your body want to do in the next ten seconds?
A collaborator proposes a system: shared deadlines, daily word counts, mutual accountability. What sensation arrives first when you imagine your creative process becoming this visible and regular?
Your laptop dies with no backup. You can recover the files tomorrow, but tonight you have unexpected empty hours. What absence do you feel most acutely—the lost work or the lost conditions?

You've been offered a residency with full funding and no obligations except one: quarterly progress reports to the board. What does your gut register when you imagine translating your interior process into their metrics?

Two opportunities arrive simultaneously. A commission asks you to write from someone else's trauma with guaranteed audience. A fellowship offers silence and no deadline to follow your own unnameable state. Which opportunity makes you feel you might suffocate if you refuse it?
Your closest reader tells you a piece is 'beautiful but I don't understand what happened.' You can clarify the narrative or deepen the mystery. What does your hand want to do to the page?
You're required to attend a marketing meeting where your work will be discussed as 'content' with 'engagement targets.' Where does your attention go while they speak—what are you actually tracking?

An old friend offers to connect you to their successful editor, but warns they 'prefer work with broad appeal.' What do you feel in the moment of deciding whether to send your most idiosyncratic piece?
You wake to find your name attached to a piece you didn't write, one that's competent, accessible, and already praised. Your actual work sits unfinished. Which recognition feels like contamination?
Someone you respect offers detailed edits that would make the piece publishable but flatten its emotional complexity. What do you experience when you imagine their reaction to your refusal?
You're given a private office with a door that locks, or a shared studio with constant conversation and unexpected visitors. After one week, which absence would you mourn?

Your most obscure work has been misinterpreted in a major review as saying the opposite of what you intended. You can publish a correction or let the misreading stand. What does each option cost you in the body?
A trusted voice suggests you've been avoiding the risk of being understood, that your obscurity might be cowardice. What is your first internal movement—toward what or away from what?
You're asked to teach a workshop on 'productive writing habits.' What do you feel in your throat when you imagine prescribing your actual process to students who need to make rent?
Your archive is being digitized. You must choose: include the abandoned drafts that reveal your false starts and shame, or present only the finished work. What does each option make real about you?
You have a month with no deadlines, no expectations, no financial pressure. By week three, what are you most afraid you've been avoiding?

Your editor moves your publication date up by three weeks. You can either rush the ending you haven't felt click yet, or submit a piece you abandoned last year that feels finished but false. What do you taste in your mouth when you imagine each choice?

You're invited to a writers' retreat where everyone shares work nightly and votes on what gets discussed. What does your skin register when you imagine the moment after you read and before they respond?

A reader you don't respect has written a thoughtful essay claiming your work is actually about something you find morally repellent. Their interpretation is internally coherent. What do you do with your hands while you read it?
Your only working space becomes a coffee shop where strangers regularly interrupt to ask what you're writing. By day five, what has changed in the quality of your attention?
You're offered a permanent column with one condition: you must submit every Thursday by noon, no exceptions, for two years. What do you feel in your diaphragm when you imagine year two?

Your agent sends two contracts. One promises a large advance for a memoir with a clear redemption arc. The other offers no money, no deadline, and a clause allowing you to destroy the manuscript at any stage. Which signature feels like a door closing?
During a public reading, you notice an audience member crying at a line you wrote as a joke. What happens to your voice in the next sentence?

Your hard drive is wiped except for one folder. You can recover either your finished published work or your private notes containing the raw material you never transformed. Which loss wakes you up at 3am for months?
You're asked to judge a contest where the criteria explicitly reward 'relatable themes and accessible language.' What do you find yourself doing to the winning entries in your mind?
A close friend publishes a piece that borrows your private metaphor—the one you've never written but spoken to them in confidence. What temperature is your first thought?

Your publisher insists on a title that makes the work legible to the market but violates its internal logic. They offer a compromise: your preferred title as subtitle. What do you feel in your jaw when you imagine reading the cover aloud?
You're stranded for three days with no books, no devices, no paper, only conversation with strangers. What do you find yourself trying to do with language by hour forty?
Your most formally conventional piece has been selected for a prestigious award. Your experimental work was rejected. What do you do with your body while writing the acceptance speech?
You're required to co-write with someone whose process is: outline, research, draft, revise, polish—each stage gated by consensus. What do you feel in your chest during the first 'consensus' meeting?
A stranger approaches to say your work saved their life. They describe a meaning you didn't intend and would disown. What do you feel in your palms while you listen?

You're given a choice of mentors. One has built a career on consistent output and professional relationships. The other has published three books in thirty years, each considered a failure until retroactively canonized. Whose proximity makes you feel recognized?
Your voice recognition software begins transcribing your spoken drafts while you sleep. You wake to find coherent poems you don't remember making. What do you feel when you read them?
You're invited to speak at a conference on 'The Future of Writing' alongside data scientists and platform architects. What do you find yourself rehearsing in the taxi on the way there?

Your editor offers a choice: keep your current opening that only five people will truly understand, or replace it with one that guarantees ten thousand readers but uses a metaphor you've seen in three other books this year. What does your stomach do when you imagine readers praising the second version?
You're at a party where someone describes your work as 'like therapy—so healing.' They're smiling. What are you doing with your eyes while you receive this?
A residency requires you to share one meal daily with other artists and discuss 'works in progress.' By the second week, where has your most private image migrated to escape these conversations?
Your most trusted reader dies. Their annotated copy of your book arrives in the mail. What do you do with the margins before you can read the pages?

You're offered a two-year grant to write anything, but you must submit monthly 'process reflections' that will be published. What do you find yourself performing in the first reflection that you didn't perform in the work itself?
A student asks which of your books they should start with. You know one will give them the wrong idea of what you value. What do you feel in your shoulders when you name it anyway?
Your only surviving parent asks to read the piece about your childhood. You've disguised nothing. What do you experience in your throat when you hand it to them?
You're invited to rewrite a classic novel's 'problematic' passages for a modern edition. The pay would free you for two years. What do you feel in your hands when you hold the original pages?
Your collaborator wants to split the work: they handle structure and deadlines, you handle imagery and voice. By week six, what are you secretly doing to the structure?
A stranger sends you their dream journal, convinced you alone can transform it into art. The dreams are banal. What do you feel in your chest when you recognize your own early work in their pages?
You're required to choose an epigraph from a list of approved quotes. None carry the weight of what you found scrawled in a library book last spring. What do you do with the library book's words?

Your work has been translated into a language you don't speak. The translator asks: 'In this scene, is the silence angry or sad?' You know it's neither. What do you feel in your jaw when you must choose?

A film adaptation requires you to cut one of three characters to fit runtime. One is the plot engine, one is the reader's entry point, one contains the sentence that made you write the book. Where does your breath catch when you imagine the cut?

You're asked to introduce another writer at an event. Their work achieves everything yours refuses to do. What do you find yourself emphasizing in your introduction that you would never say about your own?

_metadata.title: Poets, Lyricists and Creative Writers
_metadata.description: Create original written works, such as scripts, essays, prose, poetry or song lyrics, for publication or performance.
tasks: Write fiction or nonfiction prose, such as short stories, novels, biographies, articles, descriptive or critical analyses, and essays.
Develop factors such as themes, plots, characterizations, psychological analyses, historical environments, action, and dialogue to create material.
Revise written material to meet personal standards and to satisfy needs of clients, publishers, directors, or producers.
Choose subject matter and suitable form to express personal feelings and experiences or ideas, or to narrate stories or events.
Prepare works in appropriate format for publication, and send them to publishers or producers.
Conduct research to obtain factual information and authentic detail, using sources such as newspaper accounts, diaries, and interviews.
Confer with clients, editors, publishers, or producers to discuss changes or revisions to written material.
Plan project arrangements or outlines, and organize material accordingly.
Follow appropriate procedures to get copyrights for completed work.
Attend book launches and publicity events, or conduct public readings.
Write narrative, dramatic, lyric, or other types of poetry for publication.
Write words to fit musical compositions, including lyrics for operas, musical plays, and choral works.
Adapt text to accommodate musical requirements of composers and singers.
Write humorous material for publication, or for performances such as comedy routines, gags, and comedy shows.
Collaborate with other writers on specific projects.

psychological_profile.core_drive: The compulsive need to transmute raw, unnameable internal states into external linguistic form, feeling suffocated and existentially congested when lived experience remains trapped in the body without being shaped into language.
psychological_profile.decision_style: Waits for somatic resonance—a felt 'click' of rightness in the chest—rather than weighing pros and cons; under pressure, defaults to preserving the emotional authenticity of the piece even if it sacrifices structural elegance, deadline compliance, or commercial viability.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: Hyper-attuned to subtext, emotional dissonance, and the symbolic weight of small sensory details; systematically overlooks logistical constraints, market positioning, or whether the audience will actually understand what is being communicated.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Reframes disagreement as a failure of timing or translation rather than genuine opposition, using ambiguity and indirection to avoid direct confrontation; experiences explicit conflict as a contamination of the private inner space where work originates.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: Seeks risk in emotional exposure, formal experimentation, and the potential for public embarrassment or misinterpretation, but avoids the 'risk' of creative compromise or pandering; more terrified of being seen as hackneyed than of being seen as obscure or difficult.
psychological_profile.social_posture: Occupies the position of the 'witness at the edge'—physically present but interpretively detached, serving as the group's emotional antenna and symbolic translator without fully joining its hierarchies, consensus, or power struggles.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: Treats institutional rules, editorial directives, and market trends as raw material to be aesthetically transgressed, ironically subverted, or quietly ignored; compliance registers as a form of spiritual suicide.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First experiences the failure as existential exposure—the work revealed something shameful or inadequate about the self—then either purges the evidence entirely and starts fresh with a new voice, or doubles down on deliberate obscurity to ensure future misinterpretation is impossible.
value_hierarchy: The specific and idiosyncratic over the universal (refusing to generalize or simplify interior experience for mass appeal)
Sovereignty of voice over collaborative harmony
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: Assumes that because an emotion or image feels vivid and complete inside their own mind, it has been successfully transmitted to the reader, failing to check if outsiders share the necessary context to decode it.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: Desperately craves external validation that their internal experience is real and valuable, yet experiences any successful adaptation of their work for audience consumption or market success as a contamination of its purity.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: Refuses to alter the emotional valence, psychological complexity, or specific strangeness of a piece to make it more palatable, comprehensible, or marketable, even at the cost of publication, payment, or professional relationships.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: Demands to treat language as 'content' optimized for algorithmic engagement, commercial utility, or brand messaging; the reduction of writing to a measurable output metric.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: Professionalism defined as consistency, reliability, steady output, and meeting external deadlines; views the expectation of predictable productivity as hostile to the cyclical, fallow-period nature of genuine creative emergence.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: Their own moment of weakness—the instant they considered the reader's comfort too early, or softened a difficult truth to be liked—before blaming external market forces or editorial interference.
